page: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-144-lssd is an x86_64 architecture server powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor. It features 144 vCPUs across 72 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, running at a base speed of 2.3 GHz. The processor includes a 504 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX_TILE and AMX_INT8). The system is equipped with 540.0 GB of RAM, providing 3.75 GB of memory per core, and includes 9383 GB of local NVMe SSD storage distributed across 24 local drives. No GPUs are present on this instance.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 156,273.13 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 21,445.0, both placing in the top 10% of tested servers. Memory bandwidth is also highly competitive, reaching 11,520.24 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 534.35 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. The server demonstrates strong capabilities in database operations, achieving 207.97 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and a top-tier Passmark database score of 35,667.37. However, single-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance falling into the middle 50% tier.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c4-standard-144-lssd offers high resource density, combining massive compute capacity with extensive local NVMe storage. This makes it highly effective for workloads that can fully parallelize across its 144 vCPUs and benefit from fast local storage, such as large-scale database hosting, software compilation, and multi-threaded data decompression. It is also capable of handling CPU-based LLM inference, particularly for prompt processing where it achieves top-tier token throughput, though text generation speeds for larger models represent a performance tradeoff.

Lacking a GPU, it relies on advanced CPU instructions like AVX-512 and Intel AMX for acceleration. Benchmarks show top-tier multi-core CPU and memory bandwidth performance, alongside strong database and Redis throughput. However, single-core performance remains average. With 3.75 GB of RAM per core and extensive local storage, this server is designed for highly parallelized, storage-intensive workloads. It is well-suited for large-scale database operations, software compilation, multi-threaded decompression, and CPU-based LLM prompt processing.
